title: The path to Brahman (18.49–18.58)
hook: near the end, Krishna draws the whole road in ten verses
tomorrow: "I have told you. Now do as you choose." (18.59–18.66)

segments.voice: Yesterday: duty according to nature. Your line was your own dharma, imperfect, beats another's, perfect. Every fire has some smoke. Did you turn back to what's yours? Today, where that road leads. Day two hundred twenty-three.

Near the end of a long hike, someone who's walked it before often stops the group at a clearing and points. See that ridge? We came over that. See the river? We crossed it. And there, the summit. That's where we're going. It doesn't make the last stretch shorter, but suddenly the whole trail makes sense. Chapter eighteen has a passage like that. In about ten verses, Krishna draws the whole road, from ordinary work all the way to Brahman, and to love beyond it.
screen: `A CLEARING NEAR THE END.` → `THE RIDGE, THE RIVER.` → `AND THERE, THE SUMMIT.`

segments.voice: Verse forty-nine: with understanding unattached everywhere, self mastered, desire gone, a person reaches through relinquishment the highest perfection, freedom from the bind of action. Verse fifty: now hear, briefly, how the one who's reached that perfection reaches Brahman. Then the road, verses fifty-one to fifty-three. A clear understanding. Holding yourself steady with resolve. Setting aside sound and the other sense objects, putting down liking and disliking. Living simply, eating lightly, speech, body and mind held in check. Always turning to meditation, resting in dispassion. Letting go of ego, force, pride, desire, anger, and the need to own things. Free of mine, at peace. That one, Krishna says, is fit to become Brahman. The word that holds it together is dhriti, steadiness, resolve. Not a burst of effort. A steady hand. Then verse fifty-four, the summit, and a surprise. Having become Brahman, serene, that person neither grieves nor craves. The same toward all beings, they reach the highest love for me. Many expect the road to end in a merging where love disappears. Here, on becoming Brahman, love begins. Verse fifty-five: by love they know me as I truly am, and knowing me, they enter me. Advaita teachers read this as knowledge completing itself; Vaishnava teachers read it as devotion as the goal. Both keep the verse. Then Krishna turns to Arjuna. Verse fifty-seven: give all your actions to me in your mind. Verse fifty-eight: with your mind on me, by my grace you'll cross every obstacle. But if, out of ego, you won't listen, you'll be lost. That's the word today: the path to Brahman.
screen: `PERFECTION THROUGH LETTING GO.` · `STEADY: SIMPLE, QUIET, FREE OF MINE.` · `BECOMING BRAHMAN, LOVE BEGINS.` · `BY MY GRACE YOU'LL CROSS.` · then, large: `THE PATH TO BRAHMAN.`

segments.voice: Sit, and try one piece of the road: steadiness. Keep the spine upright and the breath even. When a sound comes, let it pass without liking or disliking it. When a thought of mine comes, my plans, my things, let it pass too. You're not forcing anything. Just holding steady, like a hand around a cup of water, firm but not tight. The bell holds the time.
The path to Brahman. Gita eighteen, forty-nine to fifty-eight: relinquishment, steadiness, a simple quiet life free of mine, becoming Brahman, and then the highest love.
Your line: steady. Today, when something pulls you off balance, come back to one steady breath before you respond. Day two hundred twenty-three.

howItsDone: Hindu teachers often read Gita 18.49–18.58 as a summary of the whole spiritual path, from unattached work and disciplined living to realizing Brahman and supreme devotion (para bhakti).

myth: in Gita 18.54, love disappears once a person becomes Brahman
the verse says that having become Brahman, they reach the highest love.
the road includes eating lightly and living simply
verses 51–53: a simple, quiet life, free of mine.
verse 58 warns that ego that won't listen leads to being lost
by grace you cross; out of ego, you're lost.

fork.setup: you've become Brahman, serene, the same toward all beings. what does verse 54 say comes next?
options: the highest love for the divine.
fork.reveal: the highest love. and verse 55: by love they know him as he is, and enter him.

original.note: Sanskrit: brahmabhuta, having become Brahman; the summit of the road in Gita 18.54.

trapdoor: what you thought: the path ends when you merge into the absolute.
what it means: in Gita 18.54, having become Brahman, a person reaches the highest love.
what a scholar hears: 18.54 'brahma-bhutah prasannatma... mad-bhaktim labhate param'; Advaita reads 18.55 as knowledge completing itself, Vaishnava schools read supreme bhakti as the goal.
